R-M5-1.ruling: c3 canonicalizer - strip $HIP-derived output paths, written to the PRINCIPLE (environment is not scene content), not to the karmarendersettings symptom.

R-M5-1.rule_shape: SUBSTITUTION, not line-stripping, and the evidence forced it. The composed text contains ZERO literal '$' - the variables arrive already expanded (M5b-F1). 242 of 643 lines carry the $HIP expansion, including one INSIDE a query string (&savepath=...&). Stripping those lines would blind the oracle to whether render products are authored at all and could not reach the mid-line case. Rewriting the expansion back to its token leaves every other byte intact, so a fixture that changes its output filename still changes the hash.
R-M5-1.safety_guard: Only ABSOLUTE-PATH-valued variables are substituted (_is_env_path_value). This is structural, not an optimisation: $HIPNAME expands to the bare word 'untitled' (240 hits in the composed text) and $OS expands to the NODE NAME. Substituting those by value would rewrite genuine scene content - see M5b-F2. The guard makes the dangerous case impossible rather than trusting callers.

findings.title: The composed stage carries EXPANDED environment paths - zero literal '$' - so the c3 rule cannot match on the token
findings.detail: karmarendersettings.picture is AUTHORED as '$HIP/render/$HIPNAME.$OS.$F4.exr' (unexpandedString) but reaches the flattened stage as 240 time-sampled absolute paths. lines_with_literal_dollar is EMPTY across all 643 composed lines. $HIP's expansion appears on 242 of them in three shapes: a whole value (HoudiniSavePath), a value MID-LINE inside a query string (HoudiniVolumeFilePaths ...&savepath=...&), and the 240 render-product samples. This is what made substitution-with-a-supplied-environment the only correct rule shape: a text-only rule has nothing to match, and line-stripping would drop 242 lines of real content and still miss the mid-line case.

findings.title: $HIPNAME expands to a bare word and $OS to the node name - substituting them by value would corrupt scene content
findings.detail: $HIPNAME -> 'untitled', with 240 hits in the composed text. $OS -> 'render_settings', the node's own name. A naive value->token substitution over the ruling's full variable list would have rewritten every occurrence of those words, including a prim legitimately named 'untitled' and every reference to a node called render_settings - destroying exactly what the hash exists to protect. Neither is machine-local anyway: an unsaved scene is 'untitled' on every host and $OS is fixture-declared. c3 therefore substitutes only values matching an absolute-path shape, which excludes both by construction.

findings.title: $HIP and $JOB expand to the SAME directory, so substitution order is observable and must be pinned
findings.detail: Both expand to the process working directory for an unsaved scene. Whichever is applied first is the token that lands in the canonical text, so an unpinned iteration order would let the same stage hash two ways in two processes - a baseline that disagrees with itself. Ordering is sorted by (-len(value), name), which is also the only order that is correct when one path prefixes another (C:/a/b must be consumed before C:/a).

findings.title: NetworkBox.removeItem ejects cleanly but RAISES on a non-member; fitAroundContents does not re-capture
findings.detail: Signature (self, item: NetworkMovableItem) -> void on 22.0.368. After removeItem the node is still a /stage child with every authored property intact (position, comment, type, bypass) and box.nodes(recurse=False) no longer reports it - so apply converges. But removeItem on a NON-member raises hou.OperationFailed, which is why the eject pass reads the membership set by name first. Separately: box.fitAroundContents() does NOT re-capture an ejected node even when it is positioned inside the box's rectangle - membership is explicit, not spatial - so the cosmetic fit at the end of an apply cannot silently undo an ejection. That last one was the adversarial case worth probing; had it been false, R-M5-3 would have been unimplementable without dropping the fit.

findings.title: The real silent-trust hole was not the point release - an UNINJECTED in-Houdini process served H21 symbols as authority on an H22 host
findings.detail: EXPECTED_HOUDINI_VERSION is set only by synapse.host.version_injector, called from the daemon (host/daemon.py:301) and the panel (panel/synapse_panel.py:300). In any OTHER in-Houdini process it stayed None, so _running_major() returned '', _pkg_symbol_table_path() fell back to the H21 table, and _load_symbol_table compared that table against _pkg_table_version() - which READS THE SAME FILE. A guaranteed match. 33255 H21 symbols became the membership authority on a 22.0.368 host with no staleness signal at all. Note the shape: with an h22 table selected the gate already refused correctly (M5-F9's case), so the dangerous path was the one where the gate had nothing to compare. Closed by making the Houdini environment a second host-agnostic source of the running build.

findings.title: A genuinely external process still grounds against the H21 table by design - residual, and out of R-M5-4's scope
findings.detail: With no Houdini at all (stock python, CI, a farm process), _running_build() returns '' and the expected build falls back to the committed package table's own stamp - so the H21 table loads as authority and reports stale=false. That is the pre-existing posture and R-M5-4 does not touch it: there is no running build for the stamp to disagree with, so there is nothing to warn about. It is recorded because 'the gate is armed' is now true only when a Houdini is actually running. Escalated as a question rather than changed, see for_ruling.

for_ruling.question: Should scout's phantom gate REFUSE (or warn) in a genuinely external process - CI, a farm node, stock python - where there is no running Houdini and the committed H21 table currently loads as authority reporting stale=false?
for_ruling.why_escalated: Article I - a value judgement about a cost, not a fact provable from the tree. Both readings are defensible. Keeping it is what lets CI and headless tooling ground anything at all, and the H21 table is a real introspected table, merely of another major. Changing it would make the gate honest about 'authority for WHICH build' but would disarm grounding everywhere Houdini is absent, which is most of CI. R-M5-4 asked only about the running build, and outside Houdini there is no running build, so this is outside what was ruled.
for_ruling.shipped_meanwhile: Nothing. The fallback is unchanged and now recorded as M5b-F8.
